prompt: Before db had a host firewall, what could app reach on db that its job does not need?
hint: Look at the first probe.

choices.text: The database port, 5432
choices.why: The application needs the database.

choices.text: SSH
choices.why: Right. app has no reason to log in to db's machine.

choices.text: No extra port, because the zone matrix already blocked it
choices.why: The probe from app showed both ports open.

choices.text: The staff LAN, through db
choices.why: db was not routing traffic.

prompt: Why did the firewall's zone matrix not stop app from opening SSH to db?
hint: Where do the two machines sit?

choices.text: The matrix allows SSH between any two servers
choices.why: The matrix sends SSH to the servers from management.

choices.text: app connects over IPv6, which the matrix ignores
choices.why: The address family is not the reason.

choices.text: They share a segment, so the traffic never crosses the firewall
choices.why: Right. Lesson 4 said so.

choices.text: SSH is established traffic and is accepted early
choices.why: A new SSH session is not established.

prompt: Match each form of least privilege to the question it answers.
hint: The table in the section.
right_distractors: how fast may this link carry traffic

prompt: A team lead asks for SSH to every server from the whole staff LAN, in case somebody needs it one day. What does least privilege answer?
hint: What is the answer to a need that has not arrived yet?

choices.text: Grant it, with a counter so the use is visible
choices.why: A counter records the excess; it does not remove it.

choices.text: A change request and a new cell when the need is real
choices.why: Right. No wider rule written in advance.

choices.text: Grant it to the team lead's own laptop instead
choices.why: Still a privilege no current job needs.

choices.text: Refuse, since staff are denied the servers for ever
choices.why: A real need gets a change request and a cell.

prompt: db's input chain accepts one port from app's address, 192.168.20.10. Which port?
hint: The database's port.

prompt: From db, the probe to app:8080 and www:443 said blocked. Which part of db's host firewall did that?
hint: Which chain sees what the machine itself starts?

choices.text: The input chain's policy of drop
choices.why: Input sees what arrives, not what db starts.

choices.text: The central firewall's forward chain
choices.why: app is on db's segment; fw does not see it.

choices.text: The rule for 5432 from app, read backwards
choices.why: A rule matches in one direction.

choices.text: The output chain's policy of drop
choices.why: Right. Only replies and loopback leave.

prompt: A month later, db's output chain is dropping connections to an address on the internet. What does that suggest?
hint: What reason does a database have to start a connection?

choices.text: Something on db is being told to act by somebody who should not
choices.why: Right. Investigate the machine.

choices.text: The rule is too narrow and should allow the internet
choices.why: Nobody listed that destination as a need.

choices.text: A client's reply is being lost
choices.why: Replies match established and leave.

choices.text: The loopback rule is missing
choices.why: Loopback is local, not the internet.

prompt: Before turning on output filtering for a server, which of these belong on its list of connections it starts? Choose all that apply.
hint: Each is a line with a destination.

choices.text: Fetching updates
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Answering app's queries on 5432
choices.why: Those are replies, already allowed as established.

choices.text: Shipping logs to a collector
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Name resolution and time
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The administrator's SSH session from admin
choices.why: That arrives; the input chain decides it.

prompt: What does from="192.168.99.10" do at the start of a line in db's authorized_keys?
hint: Whose address is it?

choices.text: Makes db connect to the jump host
choices.why: It restricts logins; it starts nothing.

choices.text: Blocks the jump host from using the key
choices.why: It is the one place the key works.

choices.text: Accepts the key from the jump host alone
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Opens port 22 to that address in the firewall
choices.why: sshd does not write firewall rules.

prompt: With the key copied to admin2, what exit status did ssh db hostname return?
hint: The echo after it.

prompt: admin2 was allowed through db's host firewall and held the right private key. Why was it refused?
hint: Right key, wrong ...?

choices.text: The copy of the key was corrupted in transit to admin2
choices.why: The same key worked from admin.

choices.text: admin2 is outside the management segment
choices.why: It is on the management segment.

choices.text: sshd refuses a key used twice
choices.why: Keys are reused login after login.

choices.text: The key is tied to the jump host's address
choices.why: Right. The place was wrong.

prompt: Why does the key also carry no-agent-forwarding and no-port-forwarding?
hint: What would each let a login become?

choices.text: They make the session faster
choices.why: Speed is not the point.

choices.text: Each turns one login into a path onward
choices.why: Right. Administration rarely needs them.

choices.text: ssh-ed25519 keys refuse to work with forwarding on
choices.why: The key type allows forwarding.

choices.text: They replace the from= restriction when the address changes
choices.why: They add to it; the two are separate.

prompt: The jump host is also called a ___: one hardened machine where every administrative session starts.
hint: The other name in the section.

prompt: According to the lesson, what is the most common excess privilege?
hint: It is not a rule written too wide.

choices.text: A rule written for a whole subnet instead of one address
choices.why: The section says the common one is different.

choices.text: A default policy of accept
choices.why: That is a baseline error, not the common excess.

choices.text: A rule whose reason ended
choices.why: Right. Nothing breaks, so it stays.

choices.text: A key without a from= restriction
choices.why: That is a different leak.

prompt: For how many seconds was the supplier's address 203.0.113.70 added to the vendor set?
hint: The element's timeout.

prompt: The supplier needs SSH to app again next month. What changes on fw?
hint: Which part never changes?

choices.text: A new accept rule with the supplier's address
choices.why: The rule reading @vendor is still there.

choices.text: An element added to the set, with a timeout
choices.why: Right. The rule stays as it is.

choices.text: The set's timeout flag is switched back on
choices.why: The flag stays on the set.

choices.text: The rule's comment is updated with the new date
choices.why: A comment grants no access.

prompt: Order the steps of just-in-time access.
hint: From the request to the end.
items: granted for a window, and recorded
trap: Withdrawal comes from the clock, after the window, not from somebody remembering.

prompt: After a quarter, a rule allowing 3389 from the whole staff LAN has a low counter, all from two addresses. What does the table suggest?
hint: Which row is it?

choices.text: Remove it: the access is not used
choices.why: That is the row for zero.

choices.text: Keep it and check its comment
choices.why: That is the row for a high count.

choices.text: Narrow it to those two sources
choices.why: Right. The rule is wider than its use.

choices.text: Widen the review period to a year before touching it
choices.why: A quarter already covers quarter-end reports.

prompt: Why can a week of counters mislead a review of the rule set?
hint: What runs at the end of a quarter?

choices.text: Counters reset every Sunday
choices.why: They count until somebody resets them.

choices.text: Quarter-end reports fall outside it
choices.why: Right. The period must include every legitimate use.

choices.text: A week of traffic overflows the counter
choices.why: The counters hold far more.

choices.text: Shadowed rules count double in a short period
choices.why: A shadowed rule counts zero.

prompt: What do flow records add to a rule's counter when narrowing it?
hint: A counter says how many.

choices.text: The bytes each packet carried
choices.why: A counter already has bytes.

choices.text: Whether the rule is shadowed
choices.why: That is the matrix test of lesson 18.

choices.text: The user logged in on each machine
choices.why: Flows know addresses, not users.

choices.text: Which machine pairs used it
choices.why: Right. That is what the narrower rule names.

prompt: An auditor needs to reach the file server from outside for three days next week. Which form of least privilege fits best?
hint: What should end it?

choices.text: A permanent rule for the auditor's address, removed at the next review
choices.why: That relies on somebody remembering.

choices.text: Their address in a set with a three-day timeout
choices.why: Right. The clock ends it.

choices.text: A key with from= set to the auditor's address
choices.why: That ties a key to a place, not to a time.

choices.text: Output filtering on the file server
choices.why: That limits what the server starts.

prompt: A second database, db2, is added to the servers segment beside app. Which control does the central firewall leave to db2 itself?
hint: Which traffic does fw never see?

choices.text: Blocking the staff LAN from db2
choices.why: That crosses fw, so the matrix does it.

choices.text: Allowing SSH from management
choices.why: The matrix already sends that.

choices.text: Limiting which ports app opens on db2
choices.why: Right. Same segment, so a host firewall.

choices.text: Rate-limiting traffic from the internet
choices.why: That arrives through fw.

prompt: A rule to an old reporting server has counted zero for a quarter and its owner has left. What is the safe next step?
hint: Lesson 5's way of making a change.

choices.text: Delete it at once, since zero proves it is unused
choices.why: Zero can also mean shadowed; test first.

choices.text: Leave it until a new owner approves its removal
choices.why: That is how temporary rules become permanent.

choices.text: Widen it first, so the counter starts showing whether anybody uses it
choices.why: That adds privilege to measure privilege.

choices.text: Remove it with a scheduled way back and run the matrix test
choices.why: Right. Then watch for a complaint.
